comment: Physical transport properties for alcohol electrooxidation. Diffusion coefficients are INFINITE DILUTION values in pure water at 25°C (cgs: cm²/s). These must be corrected for real electrolyte conditions using the Wilke-Chang or Stokes-Einstein equation. Kinematic viscosities are for electrolyte solutions (cm²/s).
_unit_warning: All diffusion coefficients are infinite-dilution values in pure water. In 1 M KOH/H2SO4, effective D can be 5-15x lower. Use only with Levich/Cottrell corrections or supply custom_D.

diffusion_infinite_dilution_cm2_per_s._reference: Derlacki et al. J.Phys.Chem 1985; Lee & Li JCED 1991; CRC Handbook 2007

2-propanol._electrochemical_note: Infinite-dilution value in pure water. In 1 M KOH on Pd electrode, effective D ≈ 1.04e-6 cm²/s (Wang et al., Open Electrochem. J. 2010). Use custom_D for RDE/Levich calculations in alkaline media.

kinematic_viscosity_cm2_per_s._reference: Lide CRC Handbook 2007; Tesis doctoral IEI Barcelona 2015

default.note: pure water at 25°C — fallback when electrolyte is unknown

viscosity_temp_coeff_per_C._note: Linear approximation valid for 15–45°C only. For wider temperature ranges use Arrhenius: ln(η) = A + B/T. Value calibrated on dilute aqueous electrolytes.
